The problem asks for a maximal triangle-free graph with 16 vertices. A maximal triangle-free graph is one that has no triangles (i.e., no K3) and is edge-maximal: adding any missing edge would create a triangle.

The classic example is the complete bipartite graph K_{8,8}, which has 16 vertices, is triangle-free (bipartite graphs have no odd cycles), and is maximal because adding any edge within the same partition would create a triangle (since any two vertices in the same part share all vertices in the other part as common neighbors). So K_{8,8} is maximal triangle-free.

By Turán's theorem, the maximum number of edges in a triangle-free graph on n vertices is floor(n^2/4) = floor(256/4) = 64. So K_{8,8} is the extremal Turán graph T(16,2), which is the complete bipartite graph with parts as equal as possible. So it's the maximum triangle-free graph, hence maximal.
